extracted.intended_audience: administrative law scholars, regulatory commenters, policy advocates and stakeholders who submit notice-and-comment responses
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting public comments under the APA's notice-and-comment rulemaking that advance the procedural purposes of framework legislation (legitimacy, neutrality, aggregation, entrenchment of deliberation, and institutional effects). Useful for advocates, coalitions, and scholars shaping comments to serve procedural as well as substantive aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic Response to a Problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice-and-comment signals democratic accountability for agency policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for comments: Comments contribute to symbolic legitimacy by demonstrating participation. Even comments unlikely to change the rule serve this function — they show engagement and help legitimize the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutral Rules for Future Decision Making
rubrics_metrics.description: The APA structures a neutral procedural playing field for all rules and regulated parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for comments: Comments should leverage the procedure's neutrality — invoke procedural protections and frame arguments in terms of fair, neutral application of rules regardless of the commenter’s substantive preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solving Collective Action Problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Where individual stakeholders cannot effectively participate alone, the notice-and-comment procedure aggregates voices to address collective-action barriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for comments: Coalition-building and aggregated comments (e.g., joint submissions, organized campaigns) serve the procedure's collective-action-solving function by showing diffuse interests and pooling resources/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrenching Macro-Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework legislation like the APA entrenches macro-values such as deliberation, transparency, and reasoned decision-making into the regulatory process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for comments: When challenging specific agency actions, explicitly appeal to these macro-values (for example, argue that an action 'undermines the APA's commitment to reasoned decision-making') to frame objections as defending systemic norms, not merely advancing parochial positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing the Internal Balance of Power
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural rules can shift power among agencies, Congress, courts, and stakeholders; notice-and-comment is part of that institutional balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for comments: Be aware of the broader institutional context and which audiences (agency decisionmakers, Congress, courts, OMB, the public) your comment may influence; tailor content and framing to the multiple potential audiences and downstream institutional effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the comment leverage procedural neutrality regardless of substantive position?
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist item as distilled from Garrett's framework: leverage the APA's procedural neutrality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the comment invokes or relies on neutral procedural protections (e.g., equal treatment, consistent processes), rather than only advancing a particular substantive outcome; use neutral-procedure language when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the comment serve the collective-action function (aggregating voices for diffuse interests)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist item: show whether the comment helps solve collective-action problems by aggregating voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider coordinating with coalitions, submitting joint comments, including evidence of broad support or cumulative harms/benefits, and documenting difficulty individual stakeholders face in participating without aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the comment appeal to APA macro-values (deliberation, transparency, reasoned decision-making)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist item: explicitly tie arguments to the APA's overarching commitments to deliberation and reasoned governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame objections or support in terms of transparency, sufficiency of record, reasoned explanation, and procedural fairness; point to how the agency's practice aligns or conflicts with these values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the comment recognize and address multiple audiences (agency, Congress, courts, OMB)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist item: acknowledge and target the different institutional actors who may read or be influenced by the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content and framing to secondary audiences (e.g., provide legal arguments useful to courts, policy framing for Congress, cost/benefit data for OMB) and make clear the broader institutional implications of the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the comment contribute to the procedure's symbolic legitimacy by demonstrating genuine participation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist item: ensure the comment advances the symbolic-democratic function of notice-and-comment by evidencing participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if substantive change is unlikely, make clear the representativeness, sincerity, and seriousness of the submission (use clear signatories, factual testimony, documented impacts) so it bolsters the perceived legitimacy of the rulemaking process.
